answer: An ember dies without an owner, so tenure must be re-earned each epoch. Every identity needs two holders outside its own ridge to tend its ember, and one tending serves one identity, so n aliases need n separate tenders rather than one crew. Tending is priced by depth: the k-th tending an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. Each tended claim is sealed with a walnut token that records its tenders, and an audit re-walks a random ridge; an unconfirmed claim extinguishes the ember and forfeits every bond on it.
